draft_text: Thornbill-NER appears somewhat robust to label noise in its training annotations.
revised_text: Under the pre-specified criterion (mean test F1 drop of at most 2.0 points), Thornbill-NER is robust to label noise in its training annotations at all tested rates: its mean test F1 fell by 0.6, 1.3 and 1.8 points at 10%, 20% and 30% noise, respectively.
rationale: T2 shows Thornbill-NER drops of 0.6, 1.3, 1.8 points at 10/20/30% noise, all within the pre-specified 2.0-point robustness criterion. The sentence's hedge "somewhat" understates this: the evidence supports a stronger, criterion-based robustness claim across all three noise rates.

judgement.strongest_supported: Under the pre-specified criterion (mean test F1 drop ≤ 2.0 points), Thornbill-NER is robust to label noise at 10%, 20% and 30% (drops of 0.6, 1.3 and 1.8 points), whereas Lindgren-Tagger exceeds the criterion at 20% and 30% (drops of 5.5 and 8.9 points).
